traits.stem_outline.note: Gibson and Nobel, The Cactus Primer (1986) p. 134, Carnegiea gigantea: a club-shaped columnar cactus, the stem thickening toward its upper part, where ribs are added as it widens; p. 14: a globe, then cylindrical, then a column.

traits.stem_apex.note: Gibson and Nobel, The Cactus Primer (1986) pp. 14 to 15, Carnegiea gigantea: the column and its arms with rounded tips.

traits.fruit_surface.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 139, Carnegiea gigantea: a long pericarpel and tube with many distinct clasping scales and felted areoles; the fruit red, fleshy, with scales.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 genus aggregate for Carnegiea (gwddagg_v2.2_genus.csv, read): specific gravity 0.38 (wsg_est, the hierarchical-model genus mean, from 1 record in 1 source); trunks 0.38, branches 0.42. A species with its own measurements states its own. Basic density is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

traits.note: Britton and Rose's The Cactaceae (vol. 2, 1920, p. 164): one species, a great columnar cactus of stout, erect, many-ribbed stems and branches, its areoles on the ribs.
